scope: Public ASCN coverage and supporting evidence, 2018–2026. A growing research archive, not an exhaustive census of all news. English, Indonesian, Malay and Thai sources were searched. Paywalls, removed pages, search indexing and local-language coverage limit completeness.
queries: ASCN annual meeting, financing, implementation, outcomes

records.title: ASEAN-Australia collaboration on smart and sustainable city development
records.claim: Australia announced A$30 million over five years for training and technical assistance, including support for the emerging network.
records.analysis: A regional funding commitment; it is not evidence that individual ASCN projects received this amount.
records.followUp: Trace allocations, disbursements and completed city activities through donor accounts.

records.title: Indonesia expands smart city network to ASEAN
records.claim: Indonesia proposed Jakarta, Makassar and Banyuwangi for the network, alongside its national smart-city programme.
records.analysis: Membership and national ambition establish participation, not delivery attributable to ASCN.
records.followUp: Compare each city's original priorities with later project records and service results.

records.title: Opening address at the Inaugural ASEAN Smart Cities Network Meeting
records.claim: The inaugural meeting described city action plans and discussions with more than 60 potential global partners.
records.analysis: Potential partners are a pipeline, not signed deals or funded projects.
records.followUp: Identify which discussions became agreements and which agreements produced operating services.

records.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Framework
records.claim: The framework links urban development to quality of life, inclusion, governance and partnership funding.
records.analysis: The framework defines what delivery should serve. Technology deployment alone does not establish these outcomes.
records.followUp: Require service and inclusion indicators alongside each project's implementation status.

records.title: ASCN reviews work on smart cities
records.claim: The meeting adopted terms of reference, elected Singapore as shepherd and launched the Phuket Smart City White Paper.
records.analysis: Governance and knowledge products are documented outputs; the release does not measure service improvements.
records.followUp: Track adoption of the white paper and continuity of city projects across chair changes.

records.title: ASEAN Australia Smart Cities Trust Fund
records.claim: ADB records the trust fund's establishment in April 2019 and its support for planning, service delivery and financial management.
records.analysis: An operational funding mechanism supports the mandate. Its regional scope is wider than the ASCN project register.
records.followUp: Match funded activities to cities and distinguish technical assistance from capital investment.

records.title: 3rd ASEAN Smart Cities Network Annual Meeting
records.claim: The virtual meeting endorsed the M&E framework, external-partner guidelines and membership-expansion options.
records.analysis: Reporting rules were established. Their adoption does not itself validate the later self-reported project results.
records.followUp: Check whether subsequent reports publish comparable measures and evidence behind completion claims.

records.title: Smart City Working Group Meeting
records.claim: The UN described its inclusive-city programme in Sihanoukville and called for consultation, housing rights and resident participation.
records.analysis: This is related city evidence before Sihanoukville joined ASCN in 2024, not an ASCN-funded result.
records.followUp: Look for public consultation records, participation measures and safeguards against displacement.

records.title: Makatizen, smart cities, and good governance
records.claim: The author questioned surveillance-led smart-city programmes and transparency of data-sharing arrangements in the Philippines.
records.analysis: An attributed opinion identifies safeguards to examine; it is not a finding of misconduct by ASCN or every named city.
records.followUp: Request privacy impact assessments, retention rules and citizen complaint mechanisms for linked systems.

records.title: เครือข่ายเมืองอัจฉริยะอาเซียน
records.claim: Thailand reported participation in the fifth annual meeting, held online on 30 August under Cambodia's chairmanship.
records.analysis: Participation and reporting activity are documented. This article does not provide comparable city outcome measures.
records.followUp: Follow the reported priorities into the 2022 M&E register and later operating evidence.

records.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Network steps up efforts on promoting smart, sustainable cities
records.claim: The sixth meeting discussed project implementation, an investment toolkit and membership expansion with external partners.
records.analysis: The release documents coordination and toolkit development, without identifying financing closed or citizen outcomes.
records.followUp: Trace the toolkit through publication, city use and transactions completed.

records.title: Three more Thai provinces join ASEAN Smart Cities Network expanding digital reach
records.claim: Chiang Mai, Khon Kaen and Rayong joined ASCN, expanding the roster from 26 to 29 cities.
records.analysis: The article also discusses national programmes; those should not be counted automatically as ASCN achievements.
records.followUp: Assess the new members' project baselines and subsequent service delivery separately from membership growth.

records.title: Secretary-General of ASEAN attends ASEAN-Japan Smart Cities Network High Level Meeting
records.claim: The Secretary-General attended the fifth ASEAN-Japan high-level meeting in Tsukuba and encouraged stronger cooperation.
records.analysis: A bilateral meeting is documented; no project-specific output is stated in this short release.
records.followUp: Find the resulting city agreements, implementing agencies and project updates.

records.title: Ditjen Bina Adwil matangkan persiapan RI di ASEAN Smart Cities Network
records.claim: Indonesia's coordination meeting discussed JAKI, Homestay Naik Kelas, HomeCare and WA KEPO, alongside its shepherd role.
records.analysis: Named services provide follow-up leads. Their uptake and effectiveness are not quantified in this report.
records.followUp: Obtain service logs, active-user counts and before/after measures for each named programme.

records.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Network reaffirms commitment to drive smart, sustainable urban development
records.claim: The seventh meeting in Luang Prabang discussed finance, capacity building and the post-2025 agenda, including data governance needs.
records.analysis: Recurring financing and governance themes identify work still to follow through; recurrence alone does not prove failure.
records.followUp: Identify financing decisions and published data-governance safeguards resulting from the meeting.

records.title: Siem Reap Smart City Project Phase 2 to be Launched with Continued Japanese Support
records.claim: The report describes eight pilots, six being implemented and expanded, and a planned second phase with JICA support.
records.analysis: Pilot delivery is reported. Phase 2 was still a future plan at publication, and resident benefits were not measured here.
records.followUp: Confirm the second phase began and obtain waste-service and platform-use measures.

records.title: Official Release: Siem Reap Smart City Project Introduction Video
records.claim: JICA describes its 2022–2025 project, pilot work and the public Siem Reap data platform.
records.analysis: The implementing partner corroborates a project and platform, but the page is promotional and supplies no comparable impact evaluation.
records.followUp: Check platform availability, reuse and measured improvements to the pilot services.

records.title: ASCN8 tumpu ASEAN Smart City Action Plan 2026-2035
records.claim: The eighth annual meeting focused on the 2026–2035 action plan, expert exchanges and planned site visits.
records.analysis: This meeting-day report describes preparation and discussion, not proof that action-plan targets were achieved.
records.followUp: Check the adopted plan, implementation owners, deadlines and later measures.

records.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Network fosters stronger cooperation towards overcoming regional urbanisation challenges
records.claim: ASEAN's release records deliberation on the action plan, membership growth and cooperation with external partners.
records.analysis: The accessible indexed text confirms meeting activity. The direct page could not be retrieved during this review.
records.followUp: Read the adopted decisions and follow financing or delivery claims to project-level sources.

records.title: PH, DILG to Chair ASEAN Smart Cities Network in 2026: Setting the Standard for Resilient and Accountable Local Governance
records.claim: DILG reports the chairmanship handover, Cauayan's inclusion and service, command-centre and transport initiatives in Philippine cities.
records.analysis: Named projects connect news to the register. The release does not establish completed transport services or independently measured impact.
records.followUp: Check operating dates, ridership, response times and service uptake against the published project statuses.

records.title: Pemerintah Kota Denpasar Sampaikan Program Smart City pada Rapat Penambahan Daerah Anggota ASCN
records.claim: Denpasar presented social, economic and governance programmes at Indonesia's new-member assessment meeting on 11 December.
records.analysis: Candidate presentations are not membership decisions. Surabaya and Palembang also presenting does not make them current ASCN members.
records.followUp: Use the official roster to verify admission, then establish Denpasar's project and outcome baseline.

records.title: Singapore's role in city diplomacy: lessons from its leadership in developing the ASEAN Smart Cities Network
records.claim: This December 2025 research examines Singapore's city diplomacy, commercial interests and ASCN's governance model.
records.analysis: Institutional analysis helps test whose priorities shape projects. It is not a network-wide causal evaluation of citizen benefits.
records.followUp: Compare partner interests with city-defined priorities and inclusion measures.

records.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Network leads the region drive for smarter, more resilient cities
records.claim: The Philippines chaired the ninth annual meeting and Smart City Talks on 20–21 July by videoconference.
records.analysis: The public release confirms the meeting and theme. It does not confirm adoption of every proposal in the draft meeting record.
records.followUp: Compare adopted decisions and the eventual 2026 M&E report with the draft record on this platform.

records.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Network: official membership and mandate
records.claim: The official roster records 38 cities as of January 2026, including Dili, and sets out ASCN's three cooperation, project and funding objectives.
records.analysis: Membership is reconciled to the official roster. Growth is an institutional output, not a measure of improvements to city life.
records.followUp: Track outcome evidence for new members without assigning projects to cities absent from a reporting cycle.

records.title: ASCN Monitoring and Evaluation Report 2025
records.claim: The September 2025 register records 134 projects: 108 ongoing, 18 completed and eight planning. The report records adoption of ASCAP.
records.analysis: Implementation categories are self-reported status, not comparable impact measures or finance disbursement.
records.followUp: Verify completed assets are operating and measure benefits against baseline conditions.

records.title: Makassar homecare: reported service reach in the 2025 M&E report
records.claim: Dottoro'ta attended 6,973 patients in 2024 and more than 2,800 by July 2025.
records.analysis: Service reach is an output. Repeat visits, health improvements and unequal access are not resolved by these counts.
records.followUp: Obtain unique-patient measures, referral changes and access by neighbourhood.

records.title: JakPreneur: reported registrations in the 2025 M&E report
records.claim: JakPreneur recorded 405,052 MSME registrations from February 2020 through June 2025.
records.analysis: Registrations show reach, not business survival, income gains or causation by ASCN.
records.followUp: Check active participation, business survival and income against a stated baseline.
